questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to enforce end-to-end data provenance and reproducibility across hybrid multi-tenant environments, combining image signing, SBOM management, and centralized provenance tracking to guard against tampered or non-reproducible artifacts.

## Key Concepts
- End-to-end data provenance across on-prem and cloud environments
- Reproducible builds with digests tied to provenance records
- Attestation formats (SBOM via CycloneDX) and cryptographic signing (Sigstore/cosign)
- Policy-as-code (Kyverno/OPA) for admission control
- CI/CD pipeline integration (GitHub Actions) and runtime verification

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow for ML model artifact pipeline
name: Model Artifact Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths: ['models/**']

jobs:
  build-and-sign:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Build model image
        run: |
          docker build -t model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} ./models/
      
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft model-api:${GITHUB_SHA} -o cyclonedx-json > model.sbom.json
      
      - name: Sign with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Attach SBOM attestation
        run: |
          cosign attest --type cyclonedx --key cosign.key \
            --predicate model.sbom.json model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
      
      - name: Upload provenance
        run: |
          curl -X POST $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL/attestations \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
            -d '{"digest":"'$GITHUB_SHA'","sbom":"model.sbom.json","signature":"cosign"}'
```

```yaml
# Kyverno policy for admission control
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: ml-model-admission
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  rules:
    - name: verify-cosign-signature
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "Model image must be cosign-signed"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
    - name: verify-sbom-attestation
      match:
        resources:
          kinds:
            - Pod
      validate:
        message: "SBOM attestation required"
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - image: "!*"
```

## Verification Steps

**Local Verification:**
```bash
# Verify cosign signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:latest

# Verify SBOM attestation
cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:latest

# Check reproducibility digest
reproctl verify --provenance $PROVENANCE_STORE_URL
```

**CI Verification:**
```yaml
verify-attestations:
  needs: build-and-sign
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - name: Verify all attestations
      run: |
        cosign verify --key cosign.pub model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
        cosign attestation verify --type cyclonedx model-api:${GITHUB_SHA}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests foundational secure supply chain practices in a beginner-friendly manner. It mirrors real-world CI gates used in production environments around Dockerfile hygiene, image signing, SBOM generation, and registry controls. It introduces modern tools like Cosign and SBOM attestations without overwhelming complexity.

## Key Concepts

- **Dockerfile Hygiene**: Non-root USER and multi-stage builds reduce security vulnerabilities and image size
- **Container Image Signing**: Using Cosign to sign and verify container images ensures integrity
- **SBOM Attestation**: Software Bill of Materials provides transparency into image contents and dependencies
- **GitHub Actions Workflows**: Implementing gates and policy checks in CI/CD pipelines
- **Registry Allowlist**: Restricting deployments to approved registries prevents supply chain attacks

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow
name: Docker Security Gate
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Validate Dockerfile
        run: |
          # Check for non-root USER
          grep -q 'USER ' Dockerfile || exit 1
          # Check for multi-stage build
          grep -q 'FROM.*AS' Dockerfile || exit 1
      
      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }} -o spdx-json > sbom.json
      
      - name: Sign image and SBOM with Cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
          cosign attest --type spdx-json --predicate sbom.json ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
      
      - name: Verify signature and attestation
        run: |
          cosign verify ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/app:${{ github.sha }}
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```javascript
// Minimal Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate for image signature
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: K8sImageSig
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sImageSig
        listKind: K8sImageSigList
        plural: k8simagesigs
        singular: k8simagesig
  targets:
    - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
      rego: |
        package k8simagesig
        violation["image unsigned"] {
          input.review.object.kind == "Pod"
          image := input.review.object.spec.containers[_].image
          not image.endswith("@sha256:")
        }
```

```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
```

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
- Tests ability to translate governance requirements into concrete, enforceable policies and CI steps. 
- Combines data catalog metadata with image provenance and basic security gates in a beginner-friendly way.

Key Concepts
- Policy as code (Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper)
- Annotations for data governance (data-catalog.uri)
- Image provenance (digest pinning, registry allowlist)
- Basic hardening (forbidden hostNetwork/hostPath, non-privileged)
- Namespace quotas and network policies

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: governance-baseline
spec:
  rules:
  - name: require-data-catalog
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "data.catalog.uri annotation required"
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            data.catalog.uri: "?*"
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    validate:
      message: "image must be pinned with digest"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: "*@sha256:*"
  - name: disallow-risky-fields
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Pod", "Deployment", "StatefulSet"]
    prune: false
    validate:
      message: "hostNetwork/hostPath/privileged not allowed"
      pattern:
        spec:
          hostNetwork: False
        volumes: []
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates real-world expertise in supply chain security by testing the ability to tie SBOMs to runtime admission policies. It aligns with vendor-agnostic security frameworks (SLSA, SBOM) and modern GitOps deployment patterns where provenance verification is critical.

## Key Concepts

- **CycloneDX SBOMs**: Standardized software bills of materials that document container contents
- **Image digests**: SHA256 references ensuring immutable image pinning
- **Kyverno admission control**: Policy engine validating deployments at Kubernetes admission time
- **Helm chart provenance**: Ensuring charts reference verified, SBOM-backed images

## Proposed Solution

### GitHub Actions Workflow: Generate and Publish SBOMs

```yaml
name: SBOM Pipeline
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  build-and-sbom:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: anchore/sbom-action@v0
        with:
          format: cyclonedx-json
          image: ${{ github.repository }}
          output-file: sbom.json
      - run: |
          echo "${{ steps.sbom.outputs.sbom-json }}" | ghcr.io/your-org/sbom-store:latest 
            --image=${{ github.repository }}@${{ steps.build.outputs.digest }}
```

### Kyverno Policy: Enforce SBOM Presence at Admission

```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-image-sbom
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Enforce
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: validate-sbom-present
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
        - Deployment
        - StatefulSet
        - DaemonSet
    preconditions:
      any:
      - key: "{{ request.operation }}"
        operator: In
        value: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
    validate:
      message: "All container images must have an associated CycloneDX SBOM"
      foreach:
      - list: "{{ request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[] }}"
        deny:
          conditions:
          - key: "{{ element.image }}"
            operator: NotEqual
            value: ""
          - key: "{{ lookup('sbom.verify', '{{ element.image }}', 'cyclonedx') }}"
            operator: NotEqual
            value: "valid"
```

### Failing Manifest (No SBOM)

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: vulnerable-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: vulnerable-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: vulnerable-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:1.25
```

**Expected Result**: Deployment blocked with error: "All container images must have an associated CycloneDX SBOM"

### Passing Manifest (SBOM Verified)

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: verified-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: verified-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: verified-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: ghcr.io/your-org/app@sha256:a1b2c3d4e5f6...
        annotations:
          sbom.cyclonedx: "ghcr.io/your-org/app/sbom/a1b2c3d4e5f6"
```

**Expected Result**: Deployment allowed

## Testing Steps

1. **Apply Kyverno policy**: `kubectl apply -f kyverno-policy.yaml`
2. **Test failing manifest**: `kubectl apply -f deployment-no-sbom.yaml` — should be rejected
3. **Test passing manifest**: `kubectl apply -f deployment-with-sbom.yaml` — should be admitted
4. **Verify SBOM storage**: Confirm SBOMs are queryable via your SBOM service endpoint
5. **Audit logs**: Check Kyverno policy reports for enforcement details

```bash

cosign attest --key cosign.key --attestation dist/name-0.1-py3-none-any.bom.json dist/name-0.1-py3-none-any.whl
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Introduce policy-as-code for Kubernetes manifests using Conftest; beginner-friendly yet practical.

## Key Concepts
- Conftest, Rego policies
- Kubernetes manifest validation
- CI gate design and exit codes
- Policy-driven security checks

## Code Example
```rego
package main

deny[msg] {
  input.kind == "Deployment"
  some v in input.spec.template.spec.volumes
  v.hostPath != null
  msg = "hostPath volumes are forbidden"
}
deny[msg] {
  input.kind == "Deployment"
  cont := input.spec.template.spec.containers[_]
  cont.imagePullPolicy != "Always"
  msg = "imagePullPolicy must be Always"
}
deny[msg] {
  input.spec.template.spec.containers[_].securityContext.runAsNonRoot != true
  msg = "containers must run as non-root"
}
deny[msg] {
  input.spec.template.spec.containers[_].resources == null
  msg = "resources must be defined"
}
```

```bash
# CI usage
conftest test manifests/
```
